content:
Ravi: FYI I'm seeing a class of WS sessions that never fully close on our edge; clients reconnect and then resume_token is rejected -> duplicate messages for ~3s window. Happens most on our us-west edge during the new prefer-local rollout.
Jo: can you paste a minimal log trace? Is this related to the halfclose handling we tweaked last week?
Ravi: logs: ```
[2026-03-24T18:21:11Z] conn=gh12 state=HALFCLOSE recv=FIN from client
[2026-03-24T18:21:11Z] route=usw-01 lease=active resume_token=rt-789
[2026-03-24T18:21:11Z] client_reconnect attempt=1 token=rt-789 routed_to=usw-09
[2026-03-24T18:21:11Z] dispatch:event id=45 node=usw-01 status=sent
[2026-03-24T18:21:11Z] dispatch:event id=46 node=usw-09 status=sent
[2026-03-24T18:21:11Z] client_ack id=46
[2026-03-24T18:21:14Z] client_ack id=45
```
Ravi: client ack ordering shows 46 before 45; token rt-789 was still accepted by usw-09 even though usw-01 had not finished its flush.
Marcus: that sounds like our resume-token accept window isn't strictly exclusive. We intentionally relaxed exclusivity to reduce tail drops for high-churn clients. But for multiplexed flows that yields duplicate delivery.
Jo: console telemetry is noisy too. Nina, any frontend reports?
Nina (console): yes, per-route "active_streams" spikes when this happens and customers see transiently higher usage. We already got two support tickets. The console also shows weird "stale_resume" alerts from edge-bot.
edge-bot: alert: stale_resume rate > 0.5% (1m) on route=usw-09.
Jo: I'd rather avoid immediate global rollback. Proposed short fixes: 1) server-side - add a 50ms strict-resume lock for sessions that were half-closed, 2) instrument a metric stream.ws.resume_conflict, 3) console: show a transient caret and a tooltip "session resuming across nodes" when resume_conflict > threshold.
Marcus: 50ms lock may cause more dropped messages under packet loss, but should fix duplicates. Maybe only apply for sessions with multiplexing flag.
Ravi: we can detect multiplexed sessions via header X-MPX=true at handshake. We emit that in logs. I'll scope lock to X-MPX.
Jo: billing implication: duplicates could double count tokens briefly. Ops, can billing dedupe by resume_id + event_id within 10s? That would be a safe dedupe policy.
Marcus: adds complexity but doable. I'll ping billing.
DeployBot: rollout patch runtime/edge/2026-03-24/halfclose-lock -> canary(usw) started (id: d-9948).
DeployBot: canary completed: 4/4 healthy.
Ravi: after canary: resume_conflict metric dropped from 0.7% -> 0.02% for mp-x routes. Looks promising.
Nina (console): queued quick frontend change to show the "handoff in progress" badge and an explanation link. Small CSS/tooltip only.
Jo: follow-ups: Marcus to draft tradeoff doc (strict single-writer vs tail reliability), billing to confirm dedupe window, Nina to ship frontend note, Ravi to post reproducer script.
Ravi: repro script posted below in thread (small websocket client that sends two channels concurrently then simulates half-close).
Marcus: thanks. We'll monitor closely and consider widening rollout if metrics stay stable for 4h.
Nina (console): I'll also add a short status page blurb if customers start noticing spikes.
Ravi: thanks all. I'll keep logs and will add per-event checks for idempotency on the proxy side as a next step.
